title: Give the pet legacy-migration test the permanent tables it reads
description:
Closes #18

Phase 2 of `docs/ongoing-projects/object-save-fixes-and-arm-pricing.md`. Handed to review at
the tag `object-save-fixes-p2` (`115b6d846`): one test commit and the plan's record of the phase.
The three commits after the tag answer the review; head is `4fe9a1c56`.

## Cause

It is the test's fixture, not the migrations.

`create_legacy_pet_temporary_schema()` hides `pet_data`, `pet_save_objs` and `schema_migrations`
behind temporary tables and records migration 2026091007 as applied, because InnoDB refuses a
foreign key on a temporary table. `verify_pet_persistence_schema()` reads the key from
`information_schema`, which lists the permanent tables only. So
`Test_pet_persistence_legacy_schema_migration_is_idempotent` passed only on a database where
something had already put the key on the permanent `pet_save_objs`: the syntax-check boot, or
`Test_pet_live_schema_cascades_objects_and_rejects_orphans`, which runs after it in the suite.

Checked on a database built from `sql/master_schema.sql` alone, boot skipped:

- The test alone fails with one error, the missing foreign key, and leaves the permanent tables
  untouched: no key, no pet migration recorded.
- With the key added to the permanent table by hand and nothing else changed, it passes.
- The live-schema test alone runs all fifteen migrations on the permanent tables from the
  `master_schema.sql` shape; 2026091007 adds the key and the schema verifies. A fresh install's
  first boot goes through the same functions and is not affected.

## What changes

`b06a2367f`: the test runs `run_pet_persistence_migrations()` on the permanent tables before it
creates the temporary ones, and asserts that the call succeeded. The fixture's comment, which
said every fresh test database runs 2026091007 at startup, now says what the validator reads.
One file, `unittests/CuTest/test_database_persistence.c`. No change to the migrations, the
validator or `sql/master_schema.sql`.

After review:

- `bf3ad8c39`: the test's `UPDATE pet_data SET owner_id = 4294967295` runs only when the
  temporary fixture was created. Without the fixture the name is the permanent table, and the
  new migration call made that reachable whenever it failed (finding 1).
- `f879086e4`: `docs/guides/TESTING_GUIDE.md` names both pet tests that migrate the permanent
  tables, and says not to start two suites at once on a database that has not been migrated
  (finding 2).
- `4fe9a1c56`: the plan's record of the review.

## Verification

On `b06a2367f`, against a disposable `mariadb:10.11`, each run on a database freshly built from
`sql/master_schema.sql`:

- The test and the two neighbours that call `verify_pet_persistence_schema()`
  (`Test_pet_live_schema_cascades_objects_and_rejects_orphans`,
  `Test_pet_persistence_schema_rejects_incompatible_contract`), each alone with the syntax-check
  boot skipped: pass, and pass again on the same database.
- Each of the three alone after `Test_syntax_check_encounter_world_boots_and_cleans_up_once` ran
  on the database first: pass.
- All 36 tests of `test_database_persistence.c`, each alone on its own fresh database, boot
  skipped: pass.
- `./cutest` with the database tests on, first run: 2039 of 2039 pass. On master that run fails
  this one test.
- `make -j16 test`: 2039 tests pass.
- `python3 scripts/ci/local/run.py --base gitlab/master`: 33 of 33 jobs pass (344 s). The
  format, hygiene and secrets jobs pass again on `115b6d846`, which adds the plan's record only.

On `f879086e4`, after review, same setup:

- The failure states of finding 1 (key added by hand, user without CREATE, two processes started
  together, user without CREATE TEMPORARY TABLES), each with one pet row in the permanent
  `pet_data`: the test fails as before and the row keeps its `owner_id`. On `115b6d846` each
  state overwrote it.
- The test and its two neighbours, each alone on a fresh database, boot skipped: pass, and pass
  again on the same database.
- `./cutest` with the database tests on, first run on a fresh database: 2039 of 2039 pass.
- `make -j16 test`: 2039 tests pass.
- `python3 scripts/ci/local/run.py --base gitlab/master`: 33 of 33 jobs pass (266 s). The
  format, hygiene and secrets jobs pass again on `4fe9a1c56`, which adds the plan's record only.

## Not in this merge request

- The test still needs the permanent pet tables, as the live-schema test does. On an empty
  database the first migration fails and the new assertion reports it.
- Of two suites started together on a database that has not been migrated, one fails and passes
  when run again: the migration runner checks a version and records it in separate statements.
  The guide says so; every CI job has a database of its own.
- No deploy: the change is in the test suite and the testing guide only.
